title: Valid Anagram
summary: You get two strings `s` and `t`. Decide whether `t` uses exactly the same letters as `s`, each one the same number of times, possibly in a different order.
constraints: both strings hold only lowercase English letters

approaches.twist: Compare the character counts of both strings.
Sort both strings and compare them.
approaches.note: Works, but sorting takes O(n log n) time and O(n) space.

signals.meaning: Compare how often each letter appears.
At most 26 keys, so the counts take O(1) space.

constraintReading: Up to 5·10⁴ letters allows O(n) or O(n log n); only 26 possible letters keeps a count table at O(1) space.

hints.clarify: Does order matter? Does "aab" match "abb"? Count the letters of each by hand.
hints.approach: Count the letters of s, then walk t and take each letter away. A count that goes below zero means t has an extra letter.
hints.whyNot: Two pointers compare positions, but here positions do not matter, only counts.

slots.setup: Return False early when the lengths differ, then count the letters of s.
slots.loop: Go over every letter of t.
slots.update: Take one away from that letter's count.
slots.record: If a count drops below zero, return False.
slots.return: If the loop finishes, every count matched: return True.

solution.explanation: Counting s and walking t are both O(n). The counter has at most 26 keys, so the space is O(1).

related.relation: Also a hash map, but it remembers positions instead of counts.
